messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Programmatic access to Stan warnings
parts: Stan produces a number of warnings for human consumption; some of these are in the progress output (e.g., numerical problems), and for RStan, some of these are given by warnings() (e.g., divergent transitions). Is there any way in RStan to access these as objects that R code can examine? Are they stored in the stanfit object anywhere?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Programmatic access to Stan warnings
parts:
On Thursday, March 10, 2016 at 12:33:17 PM UTC-5, Kevin Van Horn wrote:
Stan produces a number of warnings for human consumption; some of these are in the progress output (e.g., numerical problems), and for RStan, some of these are given by warnings() (e.g., divergent transitions). Is there any way in RStan to access these as objects that R code can examine? Are they stored in the stanfit object anywhere?

They aren't stored in the stanfit object. There is a random file in tempdir() that numerical problems are written to, but they are not broken down by chain. The warnings() are generated based on things that are stored, namely the matrices produced by get_sampler_params().

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Programmatic access to Stan warnings
parts:
More specifically, you can do things like

> sampler_params <- get_sampler_params(fit, inc_warmup=FALSE)
> sum(sapply(sampler_params, function(x) c(x[,’n_divergent__’]))[,1])

> sampler_params <- get_sampler_params(fit, inc_warmup=FALSE)
> sum(sapply(sampler_params, function(x) c(x[,’treedepth__’]))[,1])

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: Programmatic access to Stan warnings
parts:
The desire to use warnings as a way of programmatically deciding on the quality of a run (perhaps before it is finished) is one that reaches pretty deep into the core Stan library because currently these warnings are only emitted as text strings which means programmatic use is fragile (i.e.-requires string matching or regex).  If you want this to get/stay on the agenda open an issue (stan-dev/stan), preferably with a usage example.

Krzysztof

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Programmatic access to Stan warnings
parts:
At least now at the Stan API services level the warnings are
sent to their own callback (even if that does just eventually
get piped to stdout). The next step would be to add structure
like a logger (with levels like DEBUG, WARN, ERROR, FATAL that
you'd access programatically.

- Bob
